approach: Root cause: `resolve` turns a red CI run into a bare failed record, and `runs_from_record` builds the failed `test` CheckRun with empty `failed_tests` and `output_tail`; the verifier brief renders neither, so the verifier reruns the suite. Fix at that source. (1) ci_result.rs gets `FailureDetail {failed_tests, output_tail}` and a defaulted `CiSource::failure_detail(&CiRecord) -> Option<FailureDetail>`. (2) `CiBranchSource::fetch` remembers every failed `test (shard N)` job (id, name, conclusion in failure|timed_out|cancelled, the same set as `GhClient::failing_test`) from the jobs reply it already read. `failure_detail` reads each of those logs through `api_text` and hands them to one pure function, `detail_from_job_logs`. That function strips the GitHub timestamps and runs `checks::failed_test_names` on the shard output (the `<binary> <test>` form of a local run). It adds a header line `failing units: <package> <selector>; ...`, taken from the `== shard k/n: <package> <selector>` lines (xtask/src/shard.rs:317, println in main.rs:108), and then the last 200 lines. COMPLETENESS RULE (answers finding 2): there is no job cap. Names are recorded only if at least one log yields real names. When names exist and any failed shard job was unreadable, listed no tests, or timed out or was cancelled, the list also gets a marker that can never be on a base: `<job name> (log not read)`, `<job name> (no failing tests listed)` or `<job name> (did not finish)`. If more than 50 names are found, the first 50 are kept and `(list cut at 50)` is added. If no log yields names, `failed_tests` stays empty, which is today's check-name rule. Any fetch error gives `None` or markers, never an error or a pass. (3) `run_routed_with_record` calls `ci.failure_detail` only for a CI record that is not all-passed, redacts through a new required `Exec::redact` (SnapExec uses its Redactor; a redaction error drops the detail) and attaches the result to the failed `test` check. (4) `verify::check_result_view(&CheckRun)` fills the new view fields, `failed_tests`, `failing_units` (split off the header line) and `output_tail`, only when `reused && !passed`, so the briefs of local checks stay byte-identical. The verifier brief renders the names, the units, and the clipped, quoted tail. It also gives the instruction to run only those tests with `cargo test -p <crate> <name>` unless there is a reason to run more. It explains the name form: `<binary> <test>`, where the binary is the library crate (`athena_core`), an integration-test file, or `doc-tests <crate>`. The `failing units` line gives the `-p` package and selector (`--lib`, `--test <file>`, `--doc`), so the command reads `cargo test -p athena-core --lib <test>`. It also says that a name in parentheses means the list is incomplete and the whole unit or shard must be run. (5) The `is_pre_existing` doc comment in verify.rs is updated and the CHANGELOG entry carries the reader audit. Facts settled from the snapshot: xtask/src/shard.rs:316-327 runs `cargo test --locked -p <pkg> <selector>` once per unit and does not stop at a failure, so every unit prints its own `Running` line. ci.yml has no CARGO_TERM_COLOR (grep), but ANSI stripping is kept as a defensive step. fail-fast is off (ci.yml:345) and the matrix is 6 shards. run/verification.rs:64-93 builds VerifierInputs from check_runs without returning early on a failure. No refusal or matching rule of the reading kind is added or changed, so refusal_corpus has no case to map. The log parser is a data reader and is covered by the unit tests below.

decisions.choice: Carry the detail through a defaulted `CiSource::failure_detail(&CiRecord)` called from `run_routed_with_record`, not new fields on CiRun/CiRecord.
decisions.reason: Only red reused runs need a log, so the green path makes no extra call, and no CiRun/CiRecord literal or persisted shape changes.

rejected.option: Add log fields to CiRun/CiRecord and fetch in `CiBranchSource::fetch`
rejected.why: It fetches a log on every red poll and edits many literals across tests for no gain.

rejected.option: Fetch the log in run/mod.rs after routing
rejected.why: The routed record would hold the data only after a second step, and the routing-level fake-Runner test could not show it.

decisions.choice: Remember the failed shard jobs (id, name, conclusion) in a RefCell on `CiBranchSource`, keyed by the run address, filled in `fetch` from the jobs reply.
decisions.reason: No extra runs/jobs round trips, and a record for another run returns `None`.

rejected.why: Two more API calls per red run, and the run could change between calls.

decisions.choice: Completeness first (finding 2): read the log of every failed shard job with no count cap. Add a marker name that never matches a baseline whenever names are recorded and a failed shard was unread, empty, timed out or cancelled, or the list was cut at 50. Record no names when no log yields any.
decisions.reason: `is_pre_existing` accepts a check when every listed name also failed on the base. A silently incomplete list would hide a new failure in an unread shard and tell the verifier to run only the listed tests. The markers work like `(did not finish)` in checks.rs `Section::close_into`. Empty names keep today's check-name rule, so the comparison only gets stricter, never looser.

rejected.option: Read at most 3 logs and skip errors
rejected.why: Records an incomplete list as complete, the exact hole the critic found.

rejected.option: Record no names when any log is missing
rejected.why: Throws away real information the verifier needs; a marker keeps the names and flags the gap.

decisions.choice: Use the conclusion set failure|timed_out|cancelled, as `GhClient::failing_test` does (client.rs:543-548). A timed-out or cancelled shard adds `<job> (did not finish)` even if its log gave names.
decisions.reason: A cut-off shard can hide further failures, and the set matches the existing reader.

rejected.why: Silently drops a timed-out shard, so the list looks complete when it is not.

decisions.choice: Reuse `checks::failed_test_names` on the timestamp-stripped shard output. Strip only the stamp and one space, so the 4-space indent of the `failures:` list survives.
decisions.reason: The names have the same `<binary> <test>` form as a local run, so baseline comparison compares like with like. Share the stamp-detection predicate with `failing_test_name`, but not that function, which trims lines.

rejected.option: A new ad hoc `failures:` parser in gh/client.rs
rejected.why: A second format that would never match baseline names.

decisions.choice: Make the name-to-command mapping explicit (finding 4): the header line `failing units: <package> <selector>; ...` goes on the first line of the recorded `output_tail`. `verify::check_result_view` splits it into `CheckResultView.failing_units`, and the brief explains the form and the `-p`/selector mapping.
decisions.reason: A name such as `lifecycle some_test` or `doc-tests athena_core x` does not say which `-p` package or `--test` selector to use, but the shard `== shard k/n: <pkg> <selector>` line does. CheckRun gains no field, and the brief clip cannot cut the header off because it is split first.

rejected.option: Explain the form in the brief only
rejected.why: The verifier would still guess the package and selector.
Changes an athena-data record, which is out of scope.

decisions.choice: Redact in routing through a required `Exec::redact` (SnapExec implements it with its Redactor). A redaction error records no detail.
decisions.reason: The log is data and the record is committed; the record must never hold raw text, including at the criterion-1 seam.

rejected.why: The routed record would hold raw text, and the guarantee would depend on the caller.
A future Exec could forget it and leak.

decisions.choice: Fill the new `CheckResultView` fields only for `reused && !passed`, through `verify::check_result_view(&CheckRun)`. `CheckResultView` derives Default, so the other literals in verification.rs use `..Default::default()`.
decisions.reason: The briefs of locally run failed checks stay byte-identical, and the function is the test seam for criterion 2.

rejected.option: Show the tail for every failed check
rejected.why: Changes local briefs and tests beyond the request.

decisions.choice: Keep the one-line wiring edit in crates/athena-core/src/run/verification.rs (finding 1) and say so openly.
decisions.reason: That file is the only place where CheckRuns become CheckResultViews, so the verifier cannot see the data without it. It is the 'verification brief' path that criterion 4 lists inside crates/athena-core, it is not governance, and the edit is small (the closure becomes a call to `check_result_view`, and three literals use `..Default::default()`).

rejected.option: Stuff names into `CheckRun.note`, which already reaches the view
rejected.why: It cannot carry the log tail, and the note is shown in status and the ui line, so it would clutter them.

decisions.choice: Update the doc comment of `is_pre_existing` in verify.rs and state the stricter comparison and why it is safe in the CHANGELOG (finding 3).
decisions.reason: The comment lists 'a reused result' among the cases where the check-name rule stands. After this change a reused red check with names is compared test by test; the markers and the empty-names fallback mean the comparison can only get stricter than today's wholesale pass, and the verdict rules themselves are not edited.

decisions.choice: Record caps are 200 lines and 64 KiB after redaction, with 50 names plus the `(list cut at 50)` marker. The brief clips the tail to 60 lines and 6 KiB and lists at most 30 names. Attach the detail only to the failed check named `test`, and fetch logs only for `test (` shard jobs.
decisions.reason: Bounded size in the committed record and the prompt; fmt and clippy log fetches are out of scope.

rejected.option: Fetch the log of every failed job
rejected.why: Out of scope and costs more calls.

risks.risk: A partly read set of shards is recorded as a complete list, so a new failure hides behind pre-existing names (finding 2).
risks.mitigation: Markers for unread, empty and timed-out shards, and for a cut list, never match a baseline. The criterion-3 test with two shards (one Err) and the verify.rs `is_pre_existing` assertion pin it.

risks.risk: A log fetch error, redaction error or malformed log turns a red result into an error or a pass.
risks.mitigation: Every failure path gives None or markers, which keep today's failed record. `resolve` and its outcomes are not edited. Tests cover Err, no list and redaction error.

risks.risk: Log text (secrets, large lines) reaches a committed record or the prompt.
risks.mitigation: Names and tail go through the Redactor before recording, with caps of 200 lines, 64 KiB and 50 names. The brief clips to 60 lines and 6 KiB and quotes the tail as data.

risks.risk: Names do not match baseline names, so pre-existing failures are judged as new, or the reverse.
risks.mitigation: Reuse `failed_test_names` for the same `<binary> <test>` form. verify.rs tests cover subset, superset, marker and empty names.

risks.risk: The verifier runs a wrong command from the `<binary> <test>` name (finding 4).
risks.mitigation: The units header gives the package and selector, and the brief explains the mapping. A test asserts the text.

risks.risk: The fake in run/tests.rs matches `/jobs` before the logs path, so the logs request returns the jobs JSON.
risks.mitigation: Step 10 serves the logs path first. The existing `Red` reply makes no log call, so its tests are unchanged.

risks.risk: A required `Exec::redact` or new view fields break other constructors.
risks.mitigation: Only two Exec impls and six `CheckResultView` literals exist (Grep). Default on the view and the compiler catch any miss.

risks.risk: Stricter comparison for reused red checks fails a verdict that passed before (finding 3).
risks.mitigation: It is intended and the markers make it only stricter than a wholesale pass. The doc comment and CHANGELOG state it, and the verdict rules themselves are not edited.

demonstrations.method: New test `red_reused_run_records_failing_tests_and_log_tail` in gh/tests.rs. It calls the production `crate::routing::run_routed_with_record`, with the production `GhClient::new(&runner, ..).ci_source(CI_BRANCH)` as the `ci` argument. The route covers fmt, clippy and test, and a stub `Exec` records any call and implements `redact` by calling a real Redactor. The fake `gh::Runner` (the existing `CiRunner`, extended in step 9) answers the runs query with a red run for the SHA and answers the jobs query with failed `test (shard 1)`, whose id is 77, plus a green fmt and clippy. It answers `actions/jobs/77/logs` with timestamped cargo output: a `== shard 1/6: athena-core --lib` line, a `Running unittests ... (target/debug/deps/athena_core-abc)` line, an indented `failures:` list of two tests, and `test result: FAILED. 1 passed; 2 failed`. Guards and preconditions: the record is not all-passed and the `test` check failed. The test asserts that the `test` CheckRun has passed=false and reused. It asserts failed_tests == ["athena_core tests::a", "athena_core tests::b"] and that output_tail starts with `failing units: athena-core --lib` and ends with the last log line with no timestamps. It asserts fmt and clippy have empty names, the stub Exec ran nothing, and the returned record is Some.
demonstrations.observes: The failed `test` check carries exactly the listed names and the log tail with the units header; no local check ran; fmt and clippy are untouched.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the `failure_detail` call and attach, failed_tests is empty and output_tail is "", so the equality and non-empty assertions fail. Without the log fetch, the fake is never asked for `actions/jobs/77/logs`.
demonstrations.seam: Entry point `routing::run_routed_with_record` via `GhClient::ci_source`. The fake `gh::Runner` is injected through `GhClient::new(&runner, ..)`; `CiRunner` exists in gh/tests.rs and step 9 extends it with job ids, a logs reply and an Err mode. The stub `Exec` is a new test struct, and the production `Exec::redact` is added in step 5. The parsing, tail and marker logic is production code; the fake only returns canned text.

The fake answers the `actions/jobs/<id>/logs` path before its `path.contains("/jobs")` branch. demonstrations.method: Tests named `reused_red_degrades_*` in gh/tests.rs using the same fake Runner and `run_routed_with_record`: (a) the logs call returns Err for the only failed shard: `test` is failed and reused, failed_tests is empty, output_tail is empty, and there is no panic. (b) The log has no `failures:` list: failed with empty failed_tests (a tail may be recorded). (c) Two failed shards, shard 1 with names and shard 2's log returning Err: failed_tests holds shard 1's names plus `test (shard 2) (log not read)`. A timed_out shard adds `(did not finish)`. More than 50 names yields 50 plus `(list cut at 50)`. A verify.rs test, `reused_red_incomplete_list_is_not_pre_existing`, uses a Baseline that lists shard 1's names and asserts `is_pre_existing` is false for the check with the marker and true for the same names without it. (d) A green reused run: the fake records every request path and none contains `/logs`. A routing.rs fake CiSource whose `failure_detail` counts calls shows zero calls. (e) An Exec whose `redact` errs: the detail is dropped and the check stays plain failed.

Without the markers, case (c) would hold only shard 1's names, and the verify.rs assertion that the check is not pre-existing would fail.
